title: Fly agaric
context: Fly agaric is a red or orange Amanita mushroom with white warts that is poisonous and related to the deadly Amanitas. Also called Amanita muscaria, red mushroom with white spots, toadstool. Look for red or orange cap with white warts, white gills, a ring on the stem and a bulb at the base; warts are remnants of a veil and can wash off in rain. Learn it as a warning. Toxic. Related to the deadly Amanitas.

title: Deadly galerina
context: Deadly galerina is a small brown mushroom on rotting wood that contains the same liver toxins as the death cap. Also called Galerina marginata, funeral bell, autumn skullcap. Look for small brown mushroom on rotting wood with a thin ring and rusty brown spores; cap 1 to 4 cm, sticky when wet. Learn it as a warning. Deadly. Grows on the same logs as honey mushrooms.

title: Webcaps (Cortinarius)
context: Webcaps are brown Cortinarius mushrooms with a cobweb veil, and some damage the kidneys days after eating. Also called Cortinarius, cortinarius, webcap. Look for rusty-brown spores, a web-like veil on young caps, often on the ground in woods; rusty-brown spore print. Learn it as a warning. Some are deadly to the kidneys. Never eat a brown mushroom you cannot identify.

title: Chicken of the woods
context: Chicken of the woods is a bright orange and yellow shelf fungus on trees with pores, not gills. Also called Laetiporus, sulphur shelf, chicken mushroom, Laetiporus sulphureus. Look for bright orange and yellow shelves with no gills on trees, soft when young; no gills; tiny pores underneath. Use it as an identification and look-alike lesson; only an expert who sees it in person can confirm it. Some people react badly, and growths on conifers or eucalyptus can be harmful.

title: Hen of the woods (maitake)
context: Hen of the woods is a large gray-brown clustered mushroom at the base of oaks, with pores instead of gills. Also called maitake, Grifola frondosa, sheep's head. Look for big clump of grey-brown overlapping fronds at the base of oaks; pores instead of gills. Use it as an identification and look-alike lesson; only an expert who sees it in person can confirm it.

title: Puffball
context: A giant puffball is a round white mushroom with no stem or gills that is solid white inside when young. Also called puffball, Calvatia, puffballs, Calvatia gigantea. Look for round white ball with no stem or gills; solid white inside when cut. Use it as an identification and look-alike lesson; only an expert who sees it in person can confirm it. A young Amanita looks like a puffball. Cut it open: any outline of a cap and stem means leave it.

title: Lion's mane
context: Lion's mane is a white mushroom of hanging icicle-like spines that grows on hardwood trees. Also called Hericium, bearded tooth, pom pom mushroom. Look for white hanging icicle-like spines on trees; no cap and no gills. Use it as an identification and look-alike lesson; only an expert who sees it in person can confirm it.

title: Oyster mushroom
context: The oyster mushroom is a gray-tan shelf mushroom on wood with gills running down to a short side stem. Also called Pleurotus, oyster mushrooms, tree oyster, Pleurotus ostreatus. Look for shelf-shaped grey-tan caps with gills running down to a short side stem, on wood; white to lilac spore print. Use it as an identification and look-alike lesson; only an expert who sees it in person can confirm it. Do not confuse it with other shelf fungi that have gills.

title: Turkey tail
context: Turkey tail is a thin, tough shelf fungus on dead wood with colored bands and white pores underneath. Also called Trametes versicolor, turkey tails. Look for thin tough shelves with colored concentric bands and a white pore underside; tough and leathery, not fleshy. Use it as an identification lesson. Yehsa does not give doses or remedies with wild fungi.

title: Birch polypore (razor strop)
context: Birch polypore is a rounded gray-white shelf fungus on dead birch, used historically as a razor strop and tinder. Also called razor strop, Fomitopsis betulina, birch bracket. Look for rounded grey-white shelf on dead birch; the pore side is white. Use it as an identification lesson. Yehsa does not give doses or remedies with wild fungi. Survival history only. Do not eat it.

title: Reishi (hemlock varnish shelf)
context: Reishi, or hemlock varnish shelf, is a glossy red-brown shelf fungus on hemlock and other conifers. Also called hemlock varnish shelf, Ganoderma, lingzhi, Ganoderma tsugae. Look for glossy varnished red-brown shelf on a stalk or the side of a tree; shiny, varnished-looking top. Use it as an identification lesson. Yehsa does not give doses or remedies with wild fungi.

title: Honey mushroom
context: Honey mushrooms are clusters of honey-colored capped mushrooms with a ring that grow on wood and roots. Also called Armillaria, honey fungus, bootlace fungus. Look for clusters of honey-coloured caps on wood with a ring; white spores. Use it as an identification and look-alike lesson; only an expert who sees it in person can confirm it. The deadly galerina looks like it.

title: Shaggy mane
context: Shaggy mane is a tall white shaggy-capped mushroom that melts into black ink as it ages. Also called Coprinus comatus, lawyer's wig, inky cap. Look for tall white cylinder cap with shaggy scales that melts into ink; gills turn black and dissolve from the bottom up. Use it as an identification and look-alike lesson; only an expert who sees it in person can confirm it.

title: Bolete
context: A bolete is a fleshy mushroom with a sponge of pores instead of gills under the cap. Also called Boletus, boletes, porcini, king bolete. Look for fat stem with a sponge of pores instead of gills under the cap; pores instead of gills under the cap. Use it as an identification and look-alike lesson; only an expert who sees it in person can confirm it. Red-pored and bitter ones are toxic. Do not eat on a photo.

title: Green-spored parasol
context: The green-spored parasol is a large lawn mushroom whose gills turn green with age, and it causes the most mushroom poisonings in North America. Also called Chlorophyllum molybdites, false parasol, green-spored lepiota, vomiter. Look for big scaly cap with a ring; gills turn green with age. Learn it as a warning. The most common mushroom poisoning in North America.

title: Hedgehog mushroom
context: The hedgehog mushroom is a pale orange mushroom with soft spines under the cap instead of gills. Also called Hydnum repandum, sweet tooth, hedgehog. Look for pale orange cap with soft spines instead of gills; small spines under the cap instead of gills. Use it as an identification and look-alike lesson; only an expert who sees it in person can confirm it.

title: Tinder fungus
context: Tinder fungus is a hoof-shaped gray woody shelf on birch and beech whose inner layer was used to carry fire. Also called horse hoof fungus, Fomes fomentarius, amadou, hoof fungus. Look for hoof-shaped grey woody shelf on birch and beech; used for tinder. Use it as an identification lesson. Yehsa does not give doses or remedies with wild fungi. Survival use for fire only.

title: Chaga
context: Chaga is a black, cracked, charcoal-like growth on birch that is orange-brown inside. Also called Inonotus obliquus, clinker fungus, birch conk. Look for black charcoal-like crust on birch with an orange inside; cracked black outer crust. Use it as an identification lesson. Yehsa does not give doses or remedies with wild fungi.
